configurations._comment: Serves the built bundle from dist/. Use this rather than wilson-dev when measuring network behaviour: `vite` dev serves every module unbundled, which fills the browser's 250-entry resource-timing buffer before the app has finished booting and makes any later request invisible. Run `npm run build` first.
configurations.name: wilson-preview-build

configurations._comment: BC1 (Bins on the cloud, schema + plumbing): this worktree's dev server on the bundle's port, signed in as the dev fixtures' tester (VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=tester, VITE_DEV_FIXTURES=1 in its .env.local). The Bins tab shows the fixtures' bins — the one visible change of BC1.
configurations.name: bc1-worktree

configurations._comment: BC2 (Bins on the cloud, the desktop app signed in): this worktree's dev server on the bundle's port, signed in as the dev fixtures' tester (VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=tester, VITE_DEV_FIXTURES=1 in its .env.local). The fixtures show the footage locations and the company's switch in Settings, Storage; the desktop's own file reads need the Electron app signed in to wilson-dev.
configurations.name: bc2-worktree

configurations._comment: BC3 (Bins on the cloud, the browser): this worktree's dev server on the bundle's port, signed in as the dev fixtures' tester (VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=tester, VITE_DEV_FIXTURES=1 in its .env.local). The Bins tab shows the catalogue a browser gets; `?bins=browser` on the URL makes the fixtures answer as the cloud does in a browser (no row reachable). Proven by fetching src/tools/rabbit_v0.1.0/bins/browserCatalogue.js, a BC3-only module, from it.
configurations.name: bc3-worktree

configurations._comment: V1: the SIGN-IN screens, without editing .env.local. Vite ranks a variable already in the process environment above .env files, so this sets VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN to a value the app ignores (App.jsx signs in only on the exact string tester) and the auth screens render while .env.local still says tester. Port 5246; the signed-in server stays on 5245.
configurations.name: v1-auth

configurations._comment: S4d (the Legal gate of its own: workspace managers see Legal files without a seat, migration 0092): this worktree's dev server on the bundle's port, signed in as the dev fixtures' tester (VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=tester, VITE_DEV_FIXTURES=1 in its .env.local). /rabbit is the admin, /rabbit?fixtures=member the plain member, /rabbit?fixtures=manager (new) the workspace manager with a member seat who now sees the Legal file and still not the invoice.
configurations.name: s4d-worktree

configurations._comment: GW1 (the file gateway's cloud side, migration 0093): this worktree's dev server on the bundle's port, as the dev fixtures' tester (VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=tester, VITE_DEV_FIXTURES=1 in its .env.local). App settings, Storage, File gateway renders from the fixtures' in-memory gateway cloud: /settings is the company with its NAS gateway, five viewings from outside and the trail; ?gateways=empty starts before the first gateway (Add a gateway, the token, the stories, the gateway appearing six seconds later); ?fixtures=member is a member's view.
configurations.name: gw1-worktree

configurations._comment: GW3 (the file gateway in the web app, migration 0095): this worktree's dev server on the bundle's port, as the dev fixtures' tester (VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=tester, VITE_DEV_FIXTURES=1 in its .env.local). R.A.B.B.I.T., Salt Hours, Bins plays the proxies through the fixtures' gateway stub in the page: /rabbit is the office door (no overlay); ?gateway=outside the outside door (the viewer's name, member code and the clock over the player); ?gateway=none no gateway enrolled; ?gateway=unseen a silent gateway; ?gateway=unreachable one this browser cannot reach; &missing=<clip id> a clip the gateway answers 404 for; ?gateways=nextroot the Settings card's new-certificate lines. ?gateway=real&gw=&host=&port=&renew_s=&sub= is the Playwright run against GW2's executable (scripts/gateway-playback-e2e.mjs).
configurations.name: gw3-worktree

configurations._comment: FX3 (the status banner under every item's title, the bid version bar under the project title, "Save edit as…", the Team tab's gallery): this worktree's dev server on the bundle's port, as the dev fixtures' tester. No .env.local: the switches are set in the process environment, which Vite ranks above .env files (as v1-auth does), and the Supabase URL is a placeholder on a closed local port (the client throws at import without one; the fixtures answer every read, so nothing reaches a real project). /rabbit is Salt Hours; ?fixtures=game turns levels and experiences on.
configurations.name: fx3-worktree
